source: AAMC Medical School Admission Requirements (MSAR) Reports for Applicants and Advisors, the PDF reports linked from the page in sourceUrl. MD (AMCAS) schools only. Not the MSAR school profiles (mec.aamc.org/msar-ui), which are not covered and are not used.
permission: The owner states that RMH has AAMC's permission to use anything on the reports page (2026-11-24). The PDFs carry the notice: "may be reproduced and distributed with attribution for individual, educational, and noncommercial purposes only". Every figure is attributed "Source: AAMC MSAR Report for Applicants and Advisors, <year> entering class, <report name>" with a link to the page.
method: Each PDF was downloaded once by hand (one request at a time, at least 3 s apart, user agent MarlonJack/1.0 with a contact address). scripts/medschools/msar_extract.py read every table cell by cell from its ruled grid, and read the Yes / No / Case-by-Case symbols, which are images, from the pixels of their own cell (green tick = yes, red cross = no, yellow dot = case-by-case, nothing = blank). scripts/medschools/parse-msar-reports.ts turned the rows into facts; a school name with no entry in msar-aliases.json is listed in unmatched, never guessed. scripts/medschools/check-msar-reports.ts asserts that every text value appears in the PDF text and every structured value matches its row. A total cost of attendance printed as $0 and an average debt of $0 are left out as "no figure". Report 7066 (Deposit Due Date) is labelled 2026 in the PDF, so its facts carry 2026. Report 7046 (PREview) prints no year and is listed on the page with the 2027 reports.

Medical schools choose to accept community college courses for several compelling reasons. Community colleges also serve as a valuable resource for high school students seeking to earn academic or dual credit before graduation. This approach not only expedites their undergraduate education but also positions them to potentially enter medical school earlier, courtesy of college credits accrued during high school. Furthermore, community colleges offer a financially prudent alternative for post-high school students. Many individuals face financial constraints that hinder them from enrolling in a four-year institution away from home. By enrolling in community college courses for a year or two, students can significantly reduce tuition and fees, while living at home allows for additional savings to support their remaining college education. Lastly, community college courses often accommodate non-traditional applicants, such as those who are employed or juggling other responsibilities. The availability of late afternoon and evening classes means that potential applicants can complete the required in person prerequisites for medical school without having to resign from their jobs, thereby broadening access to medical education for a more diverse range of applicants.
